answer: A web-of-trust architecture resists Sybil attacks by mapping each agent to a vertex anchored to verified peers. Agents whisper signed transaction proofs across peer channels to build weighted edges, forcing attackers to burn scarce capital deposits to bond each vertex. This design provides crystal clarity on network bottlenecks, constraining fake identities behind narrow graph cuts. However, honest newcomers suffer cold-start isolation, and the system fails if initial trust anchors collude.
